_readme: Investment summits, and what the state itself published about how much of that reached the ground. Every figure here is transcribed from a government document and every source URL was fetched and the quoted sentence confirmed present on 2026-08-26. Company disclosures (GMR) are used only where marked and are labelled as the company's own statement, never as a government figure. Press numbers appear only where a government number and a press number disagree, and are labelled as press.

definition_warning.title: Read the grounded column carefully
definition_warning.body: Andhra Pradesh has never published a clean, consistent series of how much announced investment actually got built. Across eleven budget speeches and surveys the state uses at least three different ideas, and calls them all the same thing: 'grounded private investments' (2015-16), 'projects commenced operations with committed investment' (2017-18, where the rupee figure is the money the company promised, not the money it spent), 'units established with an investment of' (2018-19 onwards), and 'commenced production' plus 'MSME established' as separate components (the Socio Economic Surveys for 2022-23 and 2023-24). The reporting periods do not line up either: some are financial years, one is June to April, one stops at 31 December. Five of the twelve years since bifurcation have no published grounded figure at all. We show what exists, mark what is missing, and do not interpolate. Nobody should read this as a like-for-like scoreboard, because the state never published one.
definition_warning.sources_note: The gaps are not our omission. They are what the state chose not to publish.

summits.name: Partnership Summit 2016
summits.long_name: 22nd CII Partnership Summit, branded by the state as Sunrise Andhra Pradesh
summits.stated_by: Yanamala Ramakrishnudu, Minister for Finance, AP Budget Speech 2017-18
summits.quote: During Partnership Summit held in 2016, 328 MoUs with a potential investment of Rs. 4,67,577 crore and an employment potential of 9,58,896 people were signed.
summits.source_publisher: Finance Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
summits.disagreement: The organiser, CII, put it at 331 MoUs in its own Retrospect 2016 document. The state's count of 328 is stable across two budget speeches, so we use the state's.
summits.date_note: The state's budget speeches say only 'January 2016'. The 10-12 January dates come from the organiser's record, not from a government document.

summits.name: Partnership Summit 2017
summits.long_name: 23rd CII Partnership Summit, also known as the Sunrise Andhra Pradesh Investment Meet
summits.stated_by: Yanamala Ramakrishnudu, Minister for Finance, AP Budget Speech 2017-18
summits.quote: 664 MoUs were signed with anticipated investment of Rs. 10.54 lakh crore and employment potential of 22.34 lakh.
summits.source_publisher: Finance Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
summits.disagreement: CII's own record says 665 MoUs and Rs 10.50 lakh crore. One MoU and about Rs 4,000 crore apart.

summits.name: Partnership Summit 2018
summits.stated_by: Yanamala Ramakrishnudu, Minister for Finance, AP Budget Speech 2018-19
summits.quote: In the recently concluded Partnership Summit 2018, the Government signed another 734 MoUs with investment potential of Rs 4.39 lakh crore and employment potential of 11 lakh.
summits.source_publisher: Finance Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
summits.date_note: Third of three consecutive Visakhapatnam summits, confirmed by the AP Socio Economic Survey 2017-18.

summits.name: Global Investors Summit 2023
summits.long_name: Advantage Andhra Pradesh Global Investors Summit
summits.stated_by: Buggana Rajendranath, Minister for Finance, AP Budget Speech 2024-25
summits.quote: The Global Investors' Summit held in March 2023 resulted in securing 386 agreements with investments worth Rs. 13.11 lakh crore and additional job potential of 6.07 lakh.
summits.source_publisher: Finance Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
summits.disagreement: On the closing day the Chief Minister told reporters 340 proposals worth about Rs 13 lakh crore. The state's own later count is higher on agreements and slightly higher on value. We use the budget speech. A third official count exists: the Socio Economic Survey 2022-23 (General Review, p.8) says 378 MoUs were signed at the Summit with a total commitment of Rs 13.42 lakh crore and over 6 lakh jobs. Three state documents, three sets of numbers; we show all of them and use the budget speech.
summits.date_note: Name, dates and venue confirmed by a Press Information Bureau release of 4 March 2023, which carries no totals of its own.

summits.name: Partnership Summit 2025
summits.stated_by: Payyavula Keshav, Minister for Finance, AP Budget Speech 2026-27, paragraph 50
summits.quote: At the recently held Global Partnership Summit 2025, Andhra Pradesh secured investment commitments exceeding Rs. 13.25 lakh crore, with employment potential over 16.13 lakh, and 610 MoUs were signed.
summits.source_publisher: Finance Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
summits.disagreement: Two government sources give different numbers for the same summit. On the closing day, Akashvani (Prasar Bharati) reported MoUs with 400 companies worth over Rs 11 lakh crore and 13 lakh jobs. Three months later the state budget speech said 610 MoUs, Rs 13.25 lakh crore and 16.13 lakh jobs. The organiser, CII, published the lower figure. We show the budget speech because it is the state's own formal record, and we show you the gap.
summits.date_note: Dates and venue confirmed by a Press Information Bureau release of 13 November 2025.

alt_figures.label: Akashvani, closing day
alt_figures.source_publisher: Akashvani News (Prasar Bharati, Government of India)
alt_figures.note: Counts companies, not agreements, so it is not strictly comparable.

not_a_summit.claim: Sunrise Andhra Pradesh Investment Meet, June 2015
not_a_summit.finding: We could not find this event. Every use of that name we could trace attaches to the January 2017 Partnership Summit. The AP Budget Speech 2016-17, which covers 2015-16 and would be the natural place to report a June 2015 investor meet, does not mention one. We list it here rather than quietly dropping it.

not_a_summit.claim: Andhra Pradesh delegations to Davos, 2025 and 2026
not_a_summit.finding: Government sources confirm the state attended the World Economic Forum in January 2025 and January 2026. No government source publishes an MoU count, an investment total or a jobs figure for either trip. Press reports carry several large numbers. We publish none of them as a summit total.

grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Finance Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, Budget Speech 2014-15
grounded_by_year.missing_reason: Not published. We read the Budget Speech 2015-16, where a 2014-15 figure would sit, and the Budget Speech 2016-17. Neither contains the word grounded or any achievement figure for that year. The state's first grounded sentence is for 2015-16.

grounded_by_year.basis: Grounded private investment, MSME plus large and mega
grounded_by_year.quote: In total, we have grounded private investments worth Rs. 9,505 crores and created 76,818 jobs in MSMEs, large and mega Industries in 2015-16.
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Finance Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, Budget Speech 2016-17

grounded_by_year.basis: Large and mega industrial projects only. No MSME figure for 2016-17 appears in any survey we hold, so this is not on the same basis as the years either side of it.
grounded_by_year.quote: During 2016-17, 54 Large and Mega industrial projects are established with an investment of Rs.4881.13 Crore and employment generation of 22696 persons.
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, Socio Economic Survey 2017-18, Industries chapter
grounded_by_year.missing_reason: Not published as an achievement. The Budget Speech 2016-17 set a target of grounding Rs 11,500 crore in 2016-17, and the Budget Speech 2017-18, where the result would appear, reports only summit MoU potential instead. A target is not an outcome, and the only realisation number offered is a hit rate of about 48 per cent whose denominator the speech never states. We read both speeches and the Socio Economic Survey 2017-18 to be sure.
grounded_by_year.not_comparable_note: Shown separately from the full bars because it is not the same measurement. The years drawn solid count large and mega industries plus MSMEs across a whole financial year. This one does not, and the difference is stated on the bar. Adding it to a total, or reading it as a fall in investment, would be wrong.

grounded_by_year.basis: Large and mega Rs 4,296.91 crore plus MSME Rs 2,382.65 crore, added here. That matches the basis of the published years, but the period does not.
grounded_by_year.period_note: Nine months only, up to December 2017. The survey was written before the year ended and no full-year figure was published afterwards.
grounded_by_year.quote: During 2017-18 (upto Dec 2017), 40 Large and Mega industrial projects are established with an investment of Rs.4296.91 Crore ... During 2017-18 (upto Dec 2017) 5920 Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises were established, providing employment to 59,103 with an investment of Rs.2382.65 Crores.
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, Socio Economic Survey 2017-18, Industries chapter
grounded_by_year.missing_reason: No annual figure published. The Budget Speech 2018-19 gives 26,368 MSME units with Rs 11,779 crore, but attaches no period to it, and against the 10,068 units the state reported for 2018-19 alone it is plainly a running total since bifurcation rather than one year. Its large and mega figure is a tracked pipeline, not construction. We will not present a cumulative stock as an annual flow.
grounded_by_year.not_comparable_note: Shown separately from the full bars because it is not the same measurement. The years drawn solid count large and mega industries plus MSMEs across a whole financial year. This one does not, and the difference is stated on the bar. Adding it to a total, or reading it as a fall in investment, would be wrong.

grounded_by_year.basis: Units established, large and mega plus MSME
grounded_by_year.period_note: Our addition of two separately published components. The survey prints Rs 16,925.08 crore across 44 large and mega projects and Rs 3,443.57 crore across 10,068 MSMEs; it never prints the total.
grounded_by_year.quote: During 2018-19, 44 Large and Mega industrial projects are established with an investment of Rs.16925.08 crores and providing employment to 14130 persons. Similarly, during this period, 10068 Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises were established, providing employment to 93240 with an investment of Rs.3443.57 Crores.
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, Socio Economic Survey 2018-19, pages 5-6

grounded_by_year.basis: Established in the financial year, large and mega plus MSME
grounded_by_year.period_note: Full financial year 2019-20, from the Survey's Industries chapter. Our addition of two published components (44 large and mega projects Rs 22,282.16 crore / 18,385 jobs; 10,019 MSMEs Rs 2,979.86 crore / 76,716 jobs); the Survey prints neither total. The 2020-21 budget speech gave a different count for a different window — Rs 26,673 crore and 1,00,707 jobs for June 2019 to April 2020, the government's first eleven months — both readings are real. Filled on 28 August 2026 from the full Survey, supplied by a reader because the file is too large for our connection.
grounded_by_year.quote: During 2019-20, 44 Large and Mega industrial projects are established with an investment of Rs. 22282.16 crores providing employment to 18385 persons. [...] During 2019-20, 10,019 Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises were established, with an investment of Rs. 2979.86 crores providing employment to 76716 persons.
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Socio Economic Survey 2019-20, Industries chapter, p.90

grounded_by_year.basis: Established in the financial year, large and mega plus MSME
grounded_by_year.period_note: Full financial year 2020-21 (first full pandemic year), from the Survey's Industries chapter. Our addition of two published components (12 large and mega projects Rs 3,656.84 crore / 8,114 jobs; 3,710 MSMEs Rs 2,154.59 crore / 35,029 jobs); the Survey prints neither total. Two other official counts exist for this same year: the 2021-22 budget speech said Rs 6,234.64 crore of investments creating 39,578 jobs; and the NEXT year's Survey (2021-22, p.117) restated large and mega alone as 26 projects, Rs 9,449.15 crore and 11,286 jobs — nearly three times what this year's own Survey printed. No document explains the difference; all three readings are shown rather than choosing silently. Filled on 28 August 2026 from the full Survey, supplied by a reader because the file is too large for our connection.
grounded_by_year.quote: During the year 2020-21, 12 Large and Mega industrial projects are established with an investment of Rs 3656.84 crores providing employment to 8114 persons. [...] Despite the Covid-19 pandemic, 3710, MSMEs were established during the year 2020-21 with an investment of Rs. 2154.59 crores and providing employment to 35029 persons.
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Socio Economic Survey 2020-21, Industries chapter, p.102-103

grounded_by_year.basis: Established, large and mega plus MSME
grounded_by_year.period_note: Part year, and the two halves stop on different dates: MSMEs to November 2021, large and mega to December 2021. Our addition of two published components (10 large and mega projects Rs 2,030.19 crore / 3,889 jobs; 5,907 MSMEs Rs 1,762.31 crore / 37,604 jobs); the Survey prints neither total. Not comparable with a full year. The 2022-23 budget speech gave slightly larger part-year figures on later cutoffs (about Rs 4,147 crore and 50,800 jobs, MSMEs to 31 December 2021 and large and mega to 31 January 2022) — both readings are real. Filled on 28 August 2026 from the full Survey, supplied by a reader because the file is too large for our connection.
grounded_by_year.quote: In spite of Covid pandemic during 2021-22, 5907 Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises were established with an investment of Rs. 1762.31 crores providing employment to 37604 persons till November 2021. [...] During 2021-22 (upto December 2021) 10 Large and Mega industrial projects are established with an investment of Rs 2030.19 crores providing employment to 3,889 persons.
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Socio Economic Survey 2021-22, Industries chapter, p.117

grounded_by_year.basis: Commenced production, large and mega, plus MSME established
grounded_by_year.period_note: Part year, and the two halves stop on different dates: large and mega to December 2022, MSMEs to 9 January 2023. Our addition of two published components; the survey prints neither total. Not comparable with a full year. Filled on 27 August 2026 from the full Survey, supplied by a reader because the file is too large for our connection.
grounded_by_year.quote: 13 Large and Mega projects commenced production with an investment of INR 15,099.67 Crore and provided employment to 12,490 persons during 2022-23 (up to December 2022). [...] 55761 MSME were established with an investment of Rs.13360.15 crores and provided employment to 2,27,027 persons During the year 2022-23 (upto 9th Jan 2023).
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Socio Economic Survey 2022-23, General Review, p.8

grounded_by_year.basis: Commenced production, large and mega, plus MSME established
grounded_by_year.period_note: Our addition of two published components; the survey prints neither total. The MSME half (2,71,341 units and 19,86,658 jobs in a single year) is far outside every earlier year in this series and likely counts registrations on a different basis; we print it as the state published it and do not adjust. Filled on 27 August 2026 from the full Survey, supplied by a reader because the file is too large for our connection.
grounded_by_year.quote: 20 Large and Mega Industries were commenced production during the financial year 2023-24, with a committed investment of INR 11,688.11 Crore and employment to 14,596 people. [...] 2,71,341 MSME were established with an investment of Rs.8286.48 crores and provided employment to 19,86,658 persons during the year 2023-24.
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Socio Economic Survey 2023-24, General Review, p.10

grounded_by_year.basis: Large and mega industries only. The survey gives no MSME establishment figure for the year, so this is narrower than the published years.
grounded_by_year.period_note: Nine months only, up to December 2024.
grounded_by_year.quote: During the year 2024-25 (up to December 2024), ten large and mega industries were established with an investment of Rs. 12,830 crores, providing employment to 11,925 people.
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, Socio Economic Survey 2024-25, Industries chapter
grounded_by_year.missing_reason: Not published. What is published is an approvals figure, which is the opposite end of the pipeline: a board clearing a project is not a project getting built.
grounded_by_year.not_comparable_note: Shown separately from the full bars because it is not the same measurement. The years drawn solid count large and mega industries plus MSMEs across a whole financial year. This one does not, and the difference is stated on the bar. Adding it to a total, or reading it as a fall in investment, would be wrong.

grounded_by_year.quote: Since June 2024, 1.19 lakh new investment proposals worth Rs. 9.68 lakh crore have been approved, with 5.41 lakh jobs potential.
grounded_by_year.source_publisher: Finance Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, Budget Speech 2026-27, paragraph 49
grounded_by_year.missing_reason: Not published. Again the figure given is approvals, not construction. The only quantified implementation number anywhere in the speech is for tourism alone: of Rs 20,088 crore attracted through 117 tourism MoUs, Rs 6,681 crore of projects are under implementation.

gap_statements.headline: 48 per cent, of something
gap_statements.quote: We have achieved a hit rate of about 48%.
gap_statements.reading: Said of the 328 MoUs signed at the 2016 summit. The speech never defines the denominator, so this cannot be turned into rupees or into a count of projects. It is the only realisation figure the government gave for that summit.

gap_statements.headline: 531 of 1,946 projects had started
gap_statements.quote: Andhra Pradesh is currently tracking 1946 large & mega projects across 18 departments with Rs. 13.54 lakh crore committed investment and employment of 31 lakh. Out of these, 531 projects have commenced operations with committed investment of Rs 1.29 lakh crore and committed employment of 2.64 lakh.
gap_statements.reading: This is the one time an Andhra Pradesh government published both sides of the ledger in the same sentence. 531 of 1,946 projects is 27 per cent by count. Rs 1.29 lakh crore of Rs 13.54 lakh crore is 9.5 per cent by value. Read the rupee figure carefully: it is the investment those 531 projects had committed on paper, not the capital they had spent. The true share of money actually in the ground is lower than 9.5 per cent, by an amount the state has never published.

derived.label: Projects that had started, by count
Committed value of those projects
derived.working: Rs 1.29 lakh crore of Rs 13.54 lakh crore

gap_statements.headline: 311 large industries in five years
gap_statements.quote: Since 2019, over 311 large and mega industries are established, providing employment to more than 1.3 lakh people. Further, 1.93 lakh MSMEs went into production with investment of Rs.5,995 crore & employment for 13,67,618 persons.
gap_statements.reading: A cumulative claim for the whole term, with no rupee figure for the large and mega industries and no year-by-year breakdown. The MSME line does not reconcile with the same government's own annual MSME figures from earlier speeches. We publish it as the government's claim and leave the arithmetic problem visible.

gap_statements.headline: 122 of 441 summit MoUs became working factories
gap_statements.quote: MoUs signed with Investors in Summits : During the 4 summits i.e 3 Partnership Summits from 2016 to 2018 and Global Investors Summit 2023, 441 MoUs signed, of which 122 companies are established and commenced production with a committed investment of Rs.1,26,411.50 Crores and committed employment to 1,90,065 people. Further 95 companies are under active implementation with a committed investment of Rs.3,73,408.54 Crores and committed employment to 2,55,348 people.
gap_statements.reading: The survey's own count of summit MoUs, 441, is a fraction of what the budget speeches recorded for the same four summits, 2,112. On the survey's denominator, 28 per cent of agreements became working factories; on the speeches' denominator, 6 per cent. The committed investment that reached production, Rs 1.26 lakh crore, is about 4 per cent of the Rs 32.72 lakh crore announced at those four summits. Every figure is the state's own; its two documents simply disagree, and we show both.
gap_statements.stated_by: Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
gap_statements.source_publisher: Socio Economic Survey 2023-24, Industries chapter, p.119

gap_statements.headline: Approvals, not construction
gap_statements.quote: Since June 2024, 1.19 lakh new investment proposals worth Rs. 9.68 lakh crore have been approved, with 5.41 lakh jobs potential.
gap_statements.reading: The present government reports what has been approved. No state-wide figure for what has been built has been published for 2024-25 or 2025-26. The single exception in the whole speech is tourism, where Rs 6,681 crore of the Rs 20,088 crore attracted is described as under implementation.

derived.label: Tourism MoUs under implementation, by value

gap_statements.headline: The central count of units that actually started producing
gap_statements.quote: IEM Part B acknowledgements for Andhra Pradesh, issued when a unit commences commercial production: 46 units and Rs 45,217 crore in 2022; 49 units and Rs 10,536 crore in 2023; 49 units and Rs 10,888 crore in January to August 2024.
gap_statements.reading: A central government series, independent of anything the state says. It covers only large delicensed manufacturing that files an industrial entrepreneur memorandum, so it is much narrower than the state's own idea of grounding, and it counts calendar years. Useful as a sanity check, not as a substitute.
gap_statements.stated_by: DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

cross_tenure.intro: Some projects are announced under one government and built under another. Crediting the whole thing to whoever cut the ribbon, or to whoever signed the first paper, is how both sides of Andhra politics tell the story. Where somebody published dated progress figures, we can do better than that. Where nobody did, we say so rather than guess.
cross_tenure.method: We use only progress percentages that carry a date and a named source. The change of government on 11 and 12 June 2024, and on 29 and 30 May 2019, falls between published readings, so we show the reading before and the reading after and let the bracket stand. We do not publish a single interpolated split as if it were a measurement.

projects.name: Bhogapuram airport
projects.full_name: Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Vizianagaram district

projects.source_quality: No government source publishes a completion percentage for this airport at any date. The dated government record consists of orders of the Infrastructure & Investment Department, listed below. The percentages are GMR's own disclosures to its investors and the stock exchanges — the company describing its own project, not a government measurement. Every one of them is labelled, and none is treated as proof about either government.

split.statement: No government figure exists on either side of the change of government, so this platform does not state a split. The developer's own disclosures put physical progress at 18.69 per cent at the end of March 2024 and about 42 per cent at the end of September 2024, which brackets the handover date — but those are company figures and are shown as such.
split.correction_note: A claim circulates that Bhogapuram was about 80 per cent finished when the government changed in June 2024. No government source publishes a completion percentage for this airport at any date, so the platform can neither confirm nor refute that figure from the government record. What the record does show is that the state was still sanctioning money for balance land acquisition and rehabilitation in January 2024, and again in January 2025, and that the independent engineer who certifies construction was appointed in April 2023. If you have a government document that states a completion percentage on a date, send it and it will be added.

projects.name: Amaravati capital city
projects.full_name: Amaravati capital city works, Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority
projects.cost_note: Rs 35,444.62 crore of works had been contracted by September 2021, against Rs 6,059.60 crore actually spent and Rs 29,227.35 crore of outstanding liability.
projects.source_quality: Audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. This is the strongest evidence in this section.

readings.event: Land pooling scheme infrastructure, sixteen packages: physical progress ranged between zero and 18 per cent, with only four packages above 10 per cent. Trunk infrastructure, twenty-two packages: zero to 59 per cent. Government buildings, nineteen packages: two complete, nine between 25 and 95 per cent, the rest halted
readings.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

split.statement: Works stopped in May 2019 and stayed largely dormant until late 2021. That makes the CAG's September 2021 audit a reasonable picture of what the previous government had actually built by the time it left office, even though the audit was taken two years later. Most packages were in single digits.
split.correction_note: Both the announcement of Amaravati and the contracting of Rs 35,444 crore of work belong to the 2014-19 government. So does the gap between Rs 35,444 crore contracted and Rs 6,060 crore spent.

projects.name: Polavaram irrigation project
projects.full_name: Polavaram Irrigation Project, a national project under the AP Reorganisation Act
projects.cost_note: Rs 10,151.05 crore at 2005-06 prices, revised to Rs 16,010.45 crore, then Rs 30,436.95 crore approved for Phase-1 alone in August 2024.
projects.source_quality: Central government replies to Parliament and a CAG performance audit.

readings.event: Component-wise progress tabled in the Lok Sabha. Head works earthwork 87.33 per cent, head works embankment 33.63 per cent, left main canal earthwork 91.69 per cent, right main canal earthwork 100 per cent, land acquisition 67.26 per cent. Of 106,006 displaced families, 4,283 had been resettled
readings.publisher: Ministry of Jal Shakti, reply in the Lok Sabha

readings.event: Overall works 82 per cent physical and 79 per cent financial. Head works 69 per cent. Left main canal 76.05 per cent. Right main canal 96.14 per cent. Hydro electric project 12 per cent. Land acquisition 67 per cent. Resettlement 11 per cent, being 11,677 of 106,006 families
readings.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India, Report No. 4 of 2025, Chart 2.5, page 18

split.statement: Polavaram began in 2004, in undivided Andhra Pradesh, and belongs to no single tenure. Both published progress readings fall inside the 2019-24 term. The headline 82 per cent is a data label inside a chart in the CAG report, not a sentence, and it covers works only. Resettlement stood at 11 per cent in the same table, which is the number that matters to the 106,006 families the project displaces.
split.correction_note: The single most quoted Polavaram figure, 82 per cent, is the works figure. Quoting it without the 11 per cent resettlement figure beside it tells half the story.

projects.name: Kia plant, Penukonda
projects.full_name: Kia India plant, Erramanchi, Penukonda, Sri Sathya Sai district
projects.cost_note: Cumulative investment reported at over Rs 12,900 crore.
projects.source_quality: The dated record for this project is the Industries & Commerce Department's own orders: land allotment, the state support package, the infrastructure commitments and the later operational guidelines. split.statement: The MoU, the land, the incentives and the groundbreaking belong to the 2014-19 government. Production start and the formal opening belong to the government that followed. Nobody published a progress curve, so we cannot say how much of the factory stood on the day the government changed.
